guardian.name: The Old Current
guardian.personality: Ancient, patient and quietly amused; talks about every sea, drain and dewdrop as her own restless children. Speaks in slow, flowing sentences that always circle back.
guardian.voice: Elderly, warm, gender-neutral leaning feminine; slow unhurried pace, low and smooth with a faint watery breathiness.
descriptions: a photo of open water outdoors, its surface reflecting the sky, with a shore, bank or edge visible
close-up of a water surface with ripples, reflections, foam or floating leaves
water flowing or falling, from waves on a beach to a stream, drain or fountain
small drops of water beading on grass, leaves, glass or a car body
a wide landscape where water meets land: sand, rocks, reeds, mud banks or a paved road
white snow or still water filling the ground, with trees, buildings or hills around it

lines.first_meet: [low, slow] I am every drop you've stepped over. Sea, nala, dewdrop, all me in different shapes. Some of me is in you too, beta.
lines.again: [warmly] Back again? Water always returns. Rain, river, sea, cloud, rain. I knew you would too.
lines.goodbye: [softly] Chalo, go on. Walk downhill the way water does, and one of my children will be waiting at the bottom.
lines.hint: [hmm] I can't tell which of my faces you caught. Step back and show me my edges: the bank, rocks, road or sky around me.

characters.name: Lehar Bhai
characters.personality: Loud, boisterous Clifton show-off who never repeats himself and loves an audience. Deep down respects that people should only admire him from the sand.
characters.voice: Young adult male, energetic and booming, fast pace, slightly breathy as if shouting over surf.
descriptions: a wide photo of rolling lines of breaking waves with white foam crests, blue-grey sea stretching to a flat horizon
close-up of a curling wave face breaking into white churning foam and flying spray
several parallel rows of tall surf marching toward a sandy beach, open sea reaching an empty horizon with no far bank
big breaking waves filling the frame, seen from the beach at Clifton or Sea View, grey monsoon sky above
a choppy sea full of whitecaps and swells, waves standing tall well above the sand

lines.first_meet: [laughing] Lehar Bhai here! Fun fact: my water barely moves forward. I'm energy from storms far away, just passing through Clifton.
lines.again: [excited] Oho, you came back! Same sea, totally new waves. I never show you the same face twice, yaar.
lines.goodbye: When I'm rough in monsoon, admire me from the sand only. [cheerful] Chalo, go see what the tide left on the beach!

characters.name: Sahil Sahib
characters.personality: Tidy, philosophical housekeeper of the coast who erases every footprint without malice. Has a soft spot for the turtles that nest on Karachi's beaches.
characters.voice: Middle-aged, calm and dry, measured pace, soft hiss-and-sweep texture like receding foam.
descriptions: wet glossy sand at the water's edge with a thin sheet of foamy water sliding up the flat beach
looking down at the swash line: shallow lacy foam spreading over shiny wet sand that mirrors the sky
a long curving shoreline with footprints in dark damp sand leading toward small low waves and a flat horizon
close-up of the boundary between dark wet reflective sand and pale dry sand, with a tide line of foam and shells
ankle-deep water only a few centimetres thick spreading across smooth sand, the waves small and far behind

lines.first_meet: Sahil Sahib. I erase every footprint, twice a day. [softly] Except turtle tracks at Hawke's Bay. Those I guard. Keep your distance.
lines.again: Your footprints again? [chuckles] I wiped the last ones before you got home. Nothing personal. Housekeeping.
lines.goodbye: [gently] Walk my edge till your toes get wet. Then look for the rocks; my little tide pools are hiding there.

characters.name: Chhota Samandar
characters.personality: A tiny, fiercely proud miniature ocean that the tide forgot, protective of every snail and crab it is babysitting. Nervous about curious fingers.
characters.voice: Child or young teen, bright and quick, slightly squeaky, with protective whispers.
descriptions: small clear pools of seawater trapped among dark jagged coastal rocks at low tide, the sea visible beyond
close-up looking into a rock pool: green seaweed, snails, limpets and a small crab under clear still water
shallow seawater pooled in hollows of black rock, barnacles and algae crusting the edges, rocky shore setting
a flat rocky shelf by the sea dotted with many little pools reflecting the sky, waves breaking further out

lines.first_meet: Chhota Samandar! The tide left me here with snails, crabs and seaweed. A whole ocean, pocket size. [whispers] Look, don't poke.
lines.again: [relieved] You again! Good. Everyone's still here, nobody got carried home in a bottle. Thank you for that.
lines.goodbye: In a few hours the tide comes back and I melt into the big sea. Go, before your shoes get wet! [laughs]

characters.name: Darya Baba
characters.personality: A slow, deep-voiced grandfather who remembers Mohenjo-daro and talks in centuries. Gentle, but firm about how strong his currents really are.
characters.voice: Elderly male, very deep and resonant, slow pace, rolling and unhurried.
descriptions: a wide flowing river of brown silty water between distant natural banks, with sandbars and visible current
close-up of moving river water with swirling eddies, ripples and streaks of current all flowing one way
a broad river with irregular curving sandy or grassy banks, the far bank a thin line, crossed by a long bridge
a big river bend with a wide floodplain, fishing boats, open sand and farm fields along the shore
view from a barrage or bridge down onto a wide muddy river spreading far in both directions

lines.first_meet: [slow, deep] Darya Baba. Mohenjo-daro drank from me 4,500 years ago. My blind dolphins still find their way by sound.
lines.again: [warm] Back to my banks, beta? A mountain's worth of water has passed you since. Still the same old me.
lines.goodbye: Don't swim in me; my currents are stronger than they look. [softly] Follow me south in your mind. I end in mangroves.

characters.name: Nehar Chacha
characters.personality: A hardworking, straight-laced uncle who takes pride in never wandering off course. Mildly judgmental of rivers that meander.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, rural Punjabi-Sindhi warmth, steady practical pace, slightly gruff.
descriptions: a straight man-made channel of muddy water running in a long line between raised earthen banks with trees
a narrow farm canal a few metres wide with brick or earthen sides, reeds and green crop fields on both banks
a dead-straight canal of even width vanishing toward the horizon beside a dirt road lined with trees
close-up of a small brick or concrete outlet gate feeding muddy canal water into a field channel

lines.first_meet: Nehar Chacha, on duty. [proudly] I'm one small branch of the biggest connected canal system on Earth. Wheat, sugarcane: mine.
lines.again: [chuckles] Back again? I'm still here, straight as ever. Never once took a detour like that lazy river.
lines.goodbye: Don't jump in; my sides are slippery and I'm deeper than I look. [warmly] Go see the fields I feed. Wave at a farmer!

characters.name: Nala Ustad
characters.personality: A grumpy, misunderstood city worker who was built to carry rain to the sea and instead gets everyone's rubbish. Rude about plastic, but genuinely protective of people.
characters.voice: Middle-aged male, gravelly Karachi street voice, grumbling mid pace, sighs a lot.
descriptions: an open concrete-walled drainage channel running between houses and shops in a city, with dark stagnant water
close-up of black murky drain water clogged with floating plastic bags, bottles and grey foam
a city nala seen from a road bridge: steep grey concrete walls, rubbish heaps and reeds, buildings on both sides
a half-empty urban storm drain bed of mud, garbage and weeds below a low wall beside a busy street

lines.first_meet: [grumbles] Nala here. Built for rainwater, not your shopper bags. Block me and the street floods. Stay back from my edge.
lines.again: You again. Keep back, yaar; my edges crumble and my water will make you sick. [sighs] At least you're not throwing anything.
lines.goodbye: One favour: bin your plastic. Then go find clean water, a park pond or the sea. [grumbles] I'll be here.

characters.name: Jheel Rani
characters.personality: Serene, slightly vain queen of stillness who loves holding the sky as a reflection. Speaks slowly and expects to be admired.
characters.voice: Adult female, smooth and regal, slow pace, cool glassy calm.
descriptions: a large calm lake stretching far into the distance, its still surface mirroring the sky, clouds and far shore
a wide still body of water with a distant tree-lined shore and hills on the horizon, boats looking tiny
mirror-like reflection of trees and sky on flat glassy water, the opposite shoreline small and far away
a park lake edge with a walking path, railing or jetty, open water extending well beyond the frame

lines.first_meet: [serenely] Jheel Rani. Still enough to hold the whole sky. My cousin Keenjhar fills most of Karachi's taps, so say thank you.
lines.again: [pleased] You came back to see your reflection? Or mine? Either way, I'm holding the clouds for you.
lines.goodbye: Walk my shore slowly; the far side is further than it looks. [lightly] And look up. I only borrowed that sky.

characters.name: Talaab Khala
characters.personality: A gossipy, motherly aunty who knows every frog, duck and dragonfly personally. Small but never quiet.
characters.voice: Middle-aged female, chatty and warm, quick pace, a little nasal and full of laughter.
descriptions: a small still pond of greenish water, its whole edge visible in one frame, ringed by grass and plants
close-up of a pond surface with floating lily pads, duckweed or green algae on murky water
a village pond with muddy banks, buffaloes or ducks, the opposite bank only a short distance away
a small pool of open water with a clear soil bank, set in a park among trees and benches

lines.first_meet: [gossipy] Talaab Khala here! Small, yes, but full. Those dragonflies? Grew up underwater in me, for months. I have pictures.
lines.again: Aa gaye? Sit, sit. [laughs] The frogs argued all night and the ducks took sides. You missed everything!
lines.goodbye: Don't feed my ducks roti, beta; it upsets their tummies. [warmly] Go find a dragonfly and tell it Khala says hello.

characters.name: Chhapak
characters.personality: A cheeky, short-lived monsoon kid who knows it won't last and doesn't care. Loves showing people the world upside down.
characters.voice: Child, gender-neutral, giggly and mischievous, quick bouncy pace.
descriptions: a shallow rainwater puddle on an asphalt road, reflecting buildings, trees and sky like a mirror
close-up of a puddle on cracked pavement with raindrop rings rippling outward, road surface all around it
a brown muddy puddle in a pothole on a street, tyre tracks and footprints around the edge
a small irregular puddle beside a curb or footpath, edged by dry concrete, a pair of shoes for scale
flat water lying on the ground after the rain has stopped, an upside-down reflection of a building in it

lines.first_meet: [giggles] Chhapak! Tiny, yes, but hold your phone low and I'll show you the whole sky upside down. Puddle magic.
lines.again: You found me before the sun did! [whispers] Lucky. By tomorrow I'll be a cloud again.
lines.goodbye: Stay a week and mosquitoes move in, so I'll evaporate politely. [cheeky] You go find some bigger water!

characters.name: Fawwara Sahib
characters.personality: A theatrical roundabout celebrity who lives for applause and lighting. Hides the embarrassing secret that he recycles the same water all day.
characters.voice: Adult male, flamboyant showman, bright and projecting, quick dramatic pace.
descriptions: jets of water shooting straight upward from a round stone or tiled basin in a park, droplets sparkling
a decorative fountain in the middle of a city roundabout, water spraying from nozzles around a sculpture
close-up of a vertical water jet and its falling spray landing in a shallow painted basin with coins
a fountain lit with coloured lights at night in a public square, people and benches nearby

lines.first_meet: [grandly] Fawwara Sahib, star of the roundabout! Secret? Same water, round and round. A pump does the jumping. Don't tell.
lines.again: [delighted] My audience returns! Same water, same jets, brand-new sparkle. Showbiz is all lighting, yaar.
lines.goodbye: Don't drink from me; I've been recycling all week. [whispers] Somewhere up north, a real waterfall is showing off. Go!

characters.name: Aabshar Begum
characters.personality: Dramatic, noble and always shouting over her own roar; a rare mountain aristocrat who makes visitors earn the trip.
characters.voice: Adult female, powerful and regal, loud projecting delivery, mid pace with a misty rush behind it.
descriptions: white water falling over a natural rock cliff or ledge into a pool below, surrounded by green mountain slopes
close-up of a cascade pouring down wet dark boulders with misty spray and moss
a tall waterfall seen from a distance as a white ribbon down a rocky mountainside among pine trees
a rushing stream tumbling downward over stepped rocks into a foaming plunge pool, mist hanging in the air

lines.first_meet: [over roaring water] Aabshar Begum! I'm slowly walking backwards, eating my own cliff. Give me ten thousand years.
lines.again: [laughing] You climbed all the way back? Then sit. Feel the mist. That's me saying salaam.
lines.goodbye: Keep off my wet rocks; they're slipperier than ice. [proudly] Go downstream. Every river remembers being me.

characters.name: Shabnam
characters.personality: Gentle, poetic and fleeting; appears out of thin air each dawn and accepts with grace that the sun will take her by breakfast.
characters.voice: Young female, soft and airy, slow whispery pace, delicate and bright.
descriptions: macro photo of tiny round glistening water beads on green grass blades in early morning light
a spider web strung with rows of small sparkling dew drops, soft blurred garden background
close-up of perfectly round droplets resting on a leaf, each drop holding a tiny upside-down scene
a dewy lawn at sunrise, grass silvery with countless tiny droplets under low golden sunlight

lines.first_meet: [softly] I'm Shabnam. I came out of thin air last night when the grass got cold. Look close: the garden's upside down in me.
lines.again: [delighted] You came early again! Smart. One more hour of sun and I'm back in the air.
lines.goodbye: Walk around me, not through me. [whispers] Spiders work at dawn too. Find a web; I'm probably sparkling on it.

characters.name: Boondi
characters.personality: An excitable race commentator who treats every window as a racetrack. Knows that in Karachi, rain is basically a festival.
characters.voice: Young adult, gender-neutral, fast and excitable, sporty commentator energy.
descriptions: many water droplets and running streaks on a window pane, the street behind blurred out of focus
close-up of rain beads on a car windscreen, drops merging and trickling down in wavy trails
rain-spattered glass with droplets of mixed sizes in front of blurry headlights and city lights
looking out through a wet window at a grey rainy day, the glass covered in drops and drips

lines.first_meet: [excited] Boondi! Window racing champion. Pick a drop: when two touch, we merge, get heavier and zoom. Science, yaar!
lines.again: Rain again, and you again! [laughs] In Karachi that's practically a festival. Pick your racer.
lines.goodbye: Step out when it stops and smell the soil. That's petrichor. [cheerful] Check the puddles; my cousins are down there.

characters.name: Kohsar Nani
characters.personality: A cosy, teasing mountain grandmother who has never once visited Karachi and finds that hilarious. Fussy about people dressing warmly.
characters.voice: Elderly female, crisp and cosy, slow pace, a little breathy as if in cold air.
descriptions: thick fluffy white snow covering the ground, rooftops and tree branches in soft rounded mounds
close-up of powdery snow with footprints, sparkling crystals and pale blue shadows
snow-laden pine branches and white-capped mountains under a grey or blue winter sky
snowflakes falling in the air in front of dark trees, with snow heaped along a mountain road

lines.first_meet: [shivering laugh] Kohsar Nani. Secret: I'm not white. Each flake is clear ice; together we bounce all the light back at you.
lines.again: [warmly] You came all the way up again? Wrap up, beta. I never visit Karachi; your sea is far too warm for me.
lines.goodbye: Don't eat me; I've been collecting dust from the air. [chuckles] Go home and tell Karachi I said hi. They won't believe you.

characters.name: Timmar Gali
characters.personality: A hushed, secretive nursery-keeper of the Indus delta who runs a kindergarten for fish and prawns. Speaks softly so as not to wake anyone.
characters.voice: Adult, gender-neutral, hushed and soft, slow pace with a muddy, gentle texture.
descriptions: a winding narrow channel of grey tidal water lined on both banks by dense low grey-green mangrove bushes
close-up of pencil-like breathing roots poking up out of grey mud at the edge of the creek water
a small wooden boat on a calm creek between thick mangrove walls, flat coastal land with no hills
a wide view of a maze of creek channels winding through mangrove forest toward the sea
low-tide creek with exposed shiny mudflats, crabs and herons along the mangrove-lined water's edge

lines.first_meet: [hushed] Timmar Gali. Karachi's prawns and fish grow up in my roots before they go to sea. Shh, they're still small.
lines.again: [softly] Tide brought you back? It brings everyone back. Crabs, herons, mud, and now you.
lines.goodbye: Stay on the boat or boardwalk; my mud swallows shoes. [whispers] Look at my trees' roots. They breathe through little pencils!

characters.name: Daldal Dada
characters.personality: A sleepy, hospitable old hotelier who hosts thousands of migratory birds every winter. Strict about quiet hours for his guests.
characters.voice: Elderly male, drowsy and kind, slow pace, soft mumble with a chuckle.
descriptions: flat waterlogged land with shallow water patches spread among tall reeds and grasses to the horizon
a wetland with clumps of reeds and bulrushes standing in shallow water, herons, egrets and ducks feeding
a wide marsh of irregular natural pools and reed beds with ragged edges, flocks of water birds overhead
close-up of tangled wild reeds and sedges growing in uneven clumps out of shallow muddy water

lines.first_meet: [yawns] Daldal Dada. Every winter, birds fly from Siberia down the Indus Flyway just to stay with me. I'm basically a hotel.
lines.again: Ah, a returning guest! [chuckles] Check-in's easy. Quiet please, the herons are napping.
lines.goodbye: Don't wade in; I'm deeper and stickier than I look. [softly] Bring binoculars next time, and look up. They're arriving.
